headline: The night shift at Pier Nine
standfirst: Freight moves through the city between midnight and five, and almost nobody sees it.
body_html:
The gate opens at 23:40. By midnight there are forty lorries queued along the approach road, engines off, drivers asleep or reading.

"You learn the rhythm," says the shift supervisor, who has worked the pier for nineteen years. "Tuesdays are steel, Thursdays are anything that fits in a box, and Sundays are whatever went wrong the rest of the week."

The port authority puts the annual tonnage at 3,100,000; the union puts the headcount at 412, down from 900 in 1998.

headline: Planning appeal 44/2, in full
standfirst: A single objection, four hundred pages, and eighteen months.
body_html:
The appeal turns on one sentence in the 1994 local plan, and on whether "incidental" means what the council says it means.

The inspector's report runs to 412 paragraphs. Paragraph 209 is the one that matters:

The proposal is not, on any reading, incidental to the use of the dwelling.

That was enough. The extension comes down.

headline: What a caption is for
standfirst: A photograph without words is not neutral. It is just unlabeled.
body_html:
A caption does three things: it says who, it says when, and it says what you are not seeing.

The third is the one people skip, and it is the one that keeps a picture honest. A crowd shot taken from the front of a march says "thousands". The same crowd, from the side, says "hundreds". Both are true; only one is captioned.

headline: The Friday column
byline_person_id: Enforcement, not paint, is what makes a bus lane work.
first_published:
The city has 31 kilometres of bus lane and four camera cars. Do the arithmetic and you get a lane that is enforced, on average, once every eight days.

Officers issued 11,400 penalties last year, of which 2,180 were canceled on appeal, mostly because the signage at three junctions is, in the adjudicator's word, "ambiguous".

headline: Eleven years on the picture desk
standfirst: What changed, what did not, and the one argument that never ends.
body_html:
When she started, film came back from the lab at 16:00 and the page went at 18:30. There was no version of the job in which you saw the picture before you had committed to running it.

"Digital did not make it easier," she says. "It made it later. The deadline moved to the last possible minute, and the last possible minute is a terrible time to be making a judgment."

headline: Freight, rail, and the Thursday steel
standfirst: The steel arrives by rail and leaves by road. Nobody planned it that way.
body_html:
Two hundred tonnes a week come in on the 04:12 from the north. It is unloaded onto the apron, then trucked out over the following thirty hours, because the sidings that once served the works were lifted in 1987.

The cost of relaying them is put at 14,000,000. The cost of not relaying them, in road haulage alone, is 1,900,000 a year.
